b: Setting ≠ hardening: setting = loss of plasticity (C₃A); hardening = strength gain (C₃S, C₂S).
Early strength → C₃S; later strength → C₂S; flash set & highest heat → C₃A; least strength role → C₄AF.
Gypsum controls setting (added at grinding); not a strength contributor.
Unsoundness is due to free lime, MgO, excess SO₃ — not due to fineness.
Finer cement: faster strength & more heat, but more shrinkage and cracking risk.
Abrams' law: strength depends on w/c (for full compaction) — not on cement content alone.
Bleeding is a form of segregation (Type 3). Laitance is the result of bleeding.
Air entrainment ↑ workability but ↓ strength; entrapped air is accidental and harmful.
Retarders increase bleeding; they do not cool concrete.
Calcium chloride is not an anti-freeze and is banned in prestressed concrete.
Creep = deformation under sustained load; shrinkage = deformation without load.
Young concrete creeps more; high humidity reduces both creep and shrinkage.
Compacting factor test suits low-workability concrete; slump test unsuitable for very dry or very wet mixes; Vee-Bee for very dry mixes.
Cube strength > cylinder strength (≈ 1.25×) because of platen restraint and lower height/width ratio.
Sulphate attack → ettringite & gypsum; best defence low-C₃A cement (Type V) + low w/c; MgSO₄ is the worst.
ASR needs all three: reactive silica + alkalis + moisture; sign = map cracking.
Carbonation lowers pH (danger to steel), it does not attack concrete strength directly; detected by phenolphthalein.
Silica fume reduces bleeding the most but increases water demand; fly ash improves workability ("ball bearing").
SSD is the reference moisture state for aggregates in mix design.
Bulking affects volume batching of sand, not weight batching; saturated sand does not bulk.
Low-heat cement ≠ quick-setting; low-heat is for dams; rapid-hardening gains strength fast but sets normally.
High-alumina cement sets slowly (initial ≈ 3.5 h) but hardens very fast (40 MPa in 1 day).
Steam-cured concrete at higher initial temperature gives lower ultimate strength.

Framework: PPRA Ordinance 2002 and Public Procurement Rules 2004 (federal); provinces have their own: Punjab PPRA Rules 2014, KPPRA Rules 2014, Sindh SPPRA Rules 2010, Balochistan BPPRA Rules 2014.
Response time (Rule 13): Not less than 15 days for national competitive bidding and 30 days for international competitive bidding, counted from first publication.
Advertisement: Above the threshold: PPRA website + newspapers (one English, one Urdu national daily); e-PADS for e-procurement.
Bid security: Not more than 5% of the estimated value (fixed amount, so as not to reveal the estimate).
Performance security: Commonly up to 10% of contract price, valid until completion/defects liability.
Bid validity extension: May be extended once, by not more than the original validity period; bidders refusing may withdraw without forfeiting bid security.
Repeat order: Not to exceed 15% of the original order value.
Bidding procedures: Single-stage one-envelope (simple works), single-stage two-envelope (technical + financial, opened separately), two-stage, two-stage two-envelope (complex/turnkey).
Evaluation: Lowest evaluated bid (not necessarily lowest price) is awarded; evaluation report published before award; grievance redressal committee for complaints.
💡 Exam point: PPRA: 15 days national / 30 days international; bid security ≤ 5%; repeat order ≤ 15%.
